text: hey everybody latterday Saints this week are reading second Nephi 2523 as a part of their program of study and this is a passage that has caused an awful lot of
religious trauma and anxiety because it has long been used as a proof text for a kind of works-based soteriology or
salvation meaning that you have to work your way to earning Grace this is what the passage says for we labor diligently
to WR to persuade our children and also our Brethren to Believe In Christ and to be reconciled to God for we know that it
is by grace that we are saved after all we can do and on the surface this would seem to be saying that we're not
actually saved by grace until we have done all we can do and that's precisely how it has been leveraged for
Generations however this is precisely the opposite of what the author intended and it's precisely the opposite of how
the earliest audiences would have interpreted this passage a few years ago I published a paper entitled second Nephi 2523 in literary and rhetorical
context in which I demonstrate that this passage would have been interpreted to mean despite all we can do and I
demonstrate that by reviewing the use of this phrase after all we can do in its
various iterations in the literature of the late 18th and the early 19th century and what I demonstrate is that it is an
idiom that was always used to mean despite all we can do and it is even commonly used in discussions about Grace
to indicate that Grace is what saves us despite all we can do so that is what the author would have intended by this
idiom and that is how the original audiences would have understood this idiom however since then the text has been renegotiated to serve other
purposes and specifically to serve as a proof text for a works-based soar ology that has been phenomenally harmful to
Youth and to adults for generations and that's a problem
